issue.title: Bug: [rsyslog] RELP forwarding in container rsyslog causes blocking syslog writes, degrading initialization performance under high log load

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

## Summary

PR #18113 switched Docker container rsyslog forwarding from UDP (`omfwd`) to RELP (`omrelp`). RELP is a TCP-based protocol that requires per-message ACKs. Under high syslog load, this creates a blocking chain that causes any container process writing to syslog to hang inside `sendto()`, significantly degrading initialization and configuration performance.

## Root Cause

RELP requires the sender to wait for a TCP ACK before sending the next message. When the host rsyslog is under load (e.g., during `config reload` or cold reboot), ACKs are delayed, which propagates back-pressure through the entire syslog stack inside the container:

```
host rsyslog slow to ACK
  → container rsyslog omrelp send queue exhausted (queue.size=20000)
    → container rsyslog stops reading from /dev/log Unix socket
      → /dev/log socket buffer fills (kernel default: 512 slots)
        → any process calling syslog() → sendto() BLOCKS
```

With the previous UDP (`omfwd`) configuration, `sendto()` returns immediately regardless of host rsyslog state — messages may be dropped under extreme load, but the caller never blocks.

## Affected Scope

`dockers/docker-base-bookworm/etc/rsyslog.conf` is the base image for **all** SONiC containers. Any initialization-heavy service is at risk during high log-load periods:

- `config reload` / cold reboot (many containers starting simultaneously)
- Large-scale interface provisioning (PortChannels, VLANs, etc.)
- FRR/LLDP convergence events
- syncd/orchagent bulk ASIC operations

resolution.title: [rsyslog] Prevent RELP backpressure from blocking containers
resolution.description:
## Why

Fixes https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/27359.

Container rsyslog forwards to the host with RELP. If host-side backpressure fills the RELP action queue, the default enqueue timeout can block rsyslog's imuxsock processing path and make service initialization callers stall in `syslog()`/`sendto()`.

## What

Set `queue.timeoutEnqueue="0"` on container RELP action queues so queue saturation drops immediately instead of blocking container syslog producers. This preserves RELP behavior while the queue has capacity, but restores the important pre-RELP property that syslog forwarding must not stall critical service startup paths under log storms.

Covered configs:

- `dockers/docker-base-bookworm/etc/rsyslog.conf`
- `dockers/docker-base-trixie/etc/rsyslog.conf`
- `dockers/docker-base-bullseye/etc/rsyslog.conf`
- `dockers/docker-platform-monitor/etc/rsyslog.conf`

## Test

- `git diff --check`
- `rsyslogd -N1` not run locally: `rsyslogd` is not installed on the worker host.
